sections.synopsis: An upper-level ridge will position over the region this evening before waning over the weekend. Areas of fog will be the main concern until the next disturbance arrives Saturday evening with light lowland rain and mountain snow showers. An active pattern will lead into next week as a series of frontal systems bring widespread precipitation, breezy winds, and the potential for minor coastal flooding.
sections.short_term:
The latest forecast remains on track this evening with no updates. An upper- level ridge axis will cross overhead tonight as conditions remain "dry" and stable. Quotations were needed for the word dry in the previous sentence as dewpoint depressions will have little to no spread. REFS model soundings are showing a stout inversion developing tonight across much of W WA. This feature in concert with surface high surface pressure and weak gradients will lead to develop of fog with freezing fog a possibility for portions of southern Puget Sound, southwest interior, and Kitsap Peninsula to name a few. Overnight lows will range between the upper 20s to upper 30s.

A foggy start to the day on Saturday but the pattern will begin to change. An upper-low will position offshore on Saturday, forming a Rex Block as it interacts with a high center in northern BC. This set up will allow for a sub 990-995 mb surface low to meander offshore the WA coast throughout much of the weekend. PoPs are favored to increase on Saturday afternoon as light lowland rain showers and mountain snow showers (snow levels around 2,500 to 3,000 ft) return to the forecast. Showers will continue into Sunday as well but the bulk of the precipitation will remain offshore before transitioning to steadier precipitation overnight along the coast and Olympic Peninsula. Precipitation amounts are not expected to be impactful. Seasonal temperatures are expected in the short-term with highs in the upper 40s to near 50 F and overnight lows in the 30s.

High astronomical tides over the weekend may bring the potential for some minor coastal flooding along the Pacific Coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca by Sunday.
sections.long_term: The aforementioned upper-low will finally get ingested into the mean flow on Monday as a broad upper-trough encompasses much of the NE PAC. Models are picking up on the potential for a well- organized frontal system deepening offshore Monday night into Tuesday. This will open up the pattern to a parade of disturbances, maintaining an active pattern into the latter half of next week. Here we could see widespread precipitation, breezy winds and possible minor coastal flooding as surface low pressure interacts with high astronomical tide along with the potential for high surf.
sections.marine:
Benign conditions with relatively light winds and seas around 5-6 ft will continue through this evening. Another round of patchy fog across the Puget Sound and interior Salish Sea will be possible again Saturday morning.

Over the coastal waters, winds will begin to increase overnight as a frontal system begins to approach the Pacific Northwest. Winds will increase Saturday morning, peaking around mid-day. East to southeast winds will reach Small Craft Advisory criteria cross most of the coastal waters and the west and central portions of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Occasional gale gusts are possible across the coastal waters, but confidence is highest in the strongest winds in the outermost waters north of James Island, where the watch was upgraded to a Gale Warning. Winds will stay below headline criteria for most of the inland waters, except over the East Strait of Juan de Fuca starting Saturday evening, where a Small Craft Advisory has been issued through early Sunday morning.

By Sunday, the low center well offshore deepens, which will increase the pressure gradients as it slowly creeps closer to the coast. Winds increase again across the coastal waters on Sunday and remain elevated through Sunday night.

A much stronger low pressure system is on track to arrive Monday into Tuesday with high confidence in strong southeasterly winds across the coastal waters and Strait of Juan de Fuca, with >80% chances for gales through Tuesday evening, as well as a 50-80% chance for storm force gusts across the outer coastal waters from late Monday through much of Tuesday. Winds will begin to ease from their peak Tuesday night into Wednesday but headlines will likely need to remain through the end of the week as low pressure systems continue to move through the area, keeping winds elevated.

Seas will rise early Saturday to around 8-13 ft, primarily from the southerly winds, before the longer period westerly swell arrives Saturday night into early Sunday, pushing seas back up to around 11- 14 ft. Seas will remain around 8-13 ft through Monday when the strong low will bring seas up to 15-20 ft by Tuesday. Ensemble guidance remains confident (60-80% chc) in seas above 20 ft, at least across the outermost coastal waters. Seas will likely remain above 12-15 ft through the end of the week as conditions remain active.

sections.synopsis: Breezy to locally strong trade winds will persist into Saturday. Quick passing showers caught up within this trade wind flow will primarily focus along windward and mauka areas. Upper ridging will nose in from the west and, along with a drier air mass settling in over the Central Pacific, assist in producing a few drier days early next week. The trade winds will gradually ease through midweek before a cold front moves through on Thanksgiving day and brings gusty northerly winds.
sections.short_term: Nudge probability of precipitation toward the National Blend Model that that shows a weak diffused band low level clouds with embedded showers currently filling in over Kauai from east to west. This band will shift south along the eastern end of the state increasing chances of showers through Saturday. Also nudged the coastal water winds towards the Rapid Refresh Forecast model which maintains small craft advisory level winds across all waters through tonight with a gradual trend down in areal coverage Saturday.
sections.prev_discussion:
Issued at 328 PM HST Fri Nov 20 2026 A strong High pressure system to the north will help drive breezy to locally strong trade winds across the state tonight into Saturday. In this flow, low level clouds and showers will be ushered into windward and mauka areas, with some spillover expected into interior and leeward areas due to the stronger trade wind flow and slightly elevated inversion levels. The greatest shower coverage can be expected during the overnight and early morning hours.

The high will gradually weaken and move east-southeast through the weekend and into early next week with weak ridging settling just north of the state on Monday, then sliding over the state by Tuesday night. In response, the trades will gradually weaken. At the same time, a drier airmass will move over the region and upper level ridging will build in from the west, leading to a somewhat drier, weakening trade wind pattern. However, there will be enough low-level moisture to support limited windward and mauka showers. Wednesday is looking like a transition day where the light winds will shift out of the west across the western end of the state and strengthen in advance of an approaching cold front.

According to the latest guidance, a cold front will move down the island chain on Thanksgiving Day, bringing gusty northerly winds and somewhat limited rainfall due to the drier airmass over the area. While both the GFS and ECMWF have been somewhat consistent in showing the front moving through sometime on Thursday into Friday over the last couple of runs, forecast confidence on the timing and strength of this frontal passage remains on the lower side as the models are struggling to resolve the synoptic features in the Pacific at that time range.
sections.marine:
Issued at 328 PM HST Fri Nov 20 2026 A robust 1033 mb high passing north of the islands will maintain fresh to locally near gale trade winds into tonight, and a Small Craft Advisory (SCA) is in effect for all waters. The high will move southeast and weaken Saturday and Sunday, causing trades to gradually ease and the SCA to eventually be scaled back to the typically windy waters around Big Island and Maui. As the subtropical ridge is displaced southward early next week, winds will decrease further, and the SCA will likely be dropped sometime Monday. The ridge will be pushed near or over the islands on Tuesday, and an approaching front will likely produce increasing southwest winds late Wednesday.

Small surf will prevail along north- and west-facing shores for the next few days followed by much larger swells next week. A tiny north swell will be overlapped by a small north-northwest that will peak on Sunday and decline on Monday. A large northwest swell will build on Tuesday and will push surf along north- and west-facing shores around High Surf Advisory thresholds into Wednesday. An extra large northwest swell is possible on Thanksgiving Day, though a front likely moving down the island chain at the same time could bring fresh northerly winds.

Strong trade winds will maintain rough surf above seasonal average along east-facing shores through Saturday. As trades decline, east shore surf will fall below seasonal average Sunday and will be very small through Wednesday. A small, long-period swell will bring a bump to south shore surf through Saturday, with mainly background level surf expected late Sunday through early next week.
